conventions: Two גַּם particles coordinating two subjects each take the English word the ASV writes for their own position: גַּם־אַתֶּם וְגַם־הַמֶּלֶךְ → *both ye and also the king* gives *both* and *also* to the two גַּם and *and* to the waw (12.14); גַּם־אַתֶּם גַּם־מַלְכְּכֶם → *both ye and your king*, with no waw, gives *and* to the second גַּם (12.25). Rule 14's correlative-pair fusion is for one connective rendered by two words and does not reach a written pair.

A subject pronoun the ASV supplies for a later verbless clause whose referent is a nominal written earlier in the same verse joins that nominal's discontinuous unit under rule 25 rather than being marked added: *He is witness* → יְהוָה (12.5), *as it was against your fathers* → יַד (12.15, where *was* is the second realization of the one הָיְתָה under rule 34). The competing added reading is named in each note.

Cleft and impersonal *it* in a verbless clause is added, and the copula goes where rule 20 sends it: to the only overt anchor free to bear it when the predicate is a finite relative clause (*It is Jehovah that appointed*, 12.6), and to the interrogative particle when it is fronted as the question auxiliary (*Is it not wheat harvest*, 12.17).
report: Read all 25 verses end to end against the candidate table and the added units. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently in a different construction (waw connectives read off the ASV, מִן → of / out of, אַחַר → after / following / followers of, לְ before an infinitive → to / in / that by what the ASV wrote); no construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license it.

Cross-verse constructions that recur were checked and agree: demonstrative phrases (12.2, 12.5, 12.8, 12.16, 12.18, 12.20) give *this*/*that* to the pronoun and leave both articles unrepresented; the two גַּם … (וְ)גַּם pairs (12.14, 12.25) give each גַּם its own written word and the waw its *and*; the two clefts/impersonal frames (12.6, 12.17) leave the dummy *it* added and put the copula on the anchor rule 20 names; the two resumed subjects (12.5 *He*, 12.15 *it*) both join the nominal written earlier in the verse under rule 25; both Hithpael יצב units take *stand still* whole.
Added units (12.3 *it*, 12.6 *It*, 12.13 *and*, 12.14 *well*, 12.17 *it*, 12.21 *then would ye go*, 12.23 *as for*) each answer to no morpheme and are not folded elsewhere in another verse.

BSB disagreements are all documented convention differences (object markers, articles, unrendered prepositions and waws, the paragogic he of חָלִילָה, the resumptive suffix of הִנָּם); none is a genuine error.

No promotion: the chapter's only novel judgments (supplied *this* joining a bare noun in 12.19; *indeed* joining the emphatic pronoun in 12.20; *Here I am* copula on the suffix in 12.3) are single occurrences with the competing reading named in the note and no corpus evidence here to carry a rule.
